name: amp-selfosc
description: Residual periodic activity on the error amplifier's internal nodes with the regulator settled and undriven -- i.e. does the amplifier's own (Rz/Cc Miller + class-AB buffer) local loop oscillate?
claim: The precondition under which sim/loop-stability/'s Bode phase and gain margins are a stability test at all: DR-0001's 'PM >= 45 deg and GM >= 10 dB' criterion is only valid when the loop gain T(s) has no right-half-plane poles, i.e. when the forward path is stable with the LDO loop broken. design/error_amp.sch keeps a LOCAL feedback loop (Rz/Cc from N1 around M2P and the class-AB gate buffer back to OUT) closed in exactly that condition, so the precondition is a design property that has to be measured, not assumed. This bench measures it in the time domain, where no phase-unwrapping convention can hide it: with EN held high and the loop settled, the peak-to-peak of the amplifier's internal BG node and of the pass gate over a late, quiet window must be at the noise floor. This bench makes NO claim about the LDO loop's own margins -- that is sim/loop-stability/'s (issue #10's) claim, and it is the claim this one is a precondition for.
analyses: meas tran bg_pp_light PP v(xdut_light.xerramp.bg) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran pg_pp_light PP v(loop_light) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran vo_pp_light PP v(vout_light) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran vo_avg_light AVG v(vout_light) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran bg_pp_heavy PP v(xdut_heavy.xerramp.bg) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran pg_pp_heavy PP v(loop_heavy) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran vo_pp_heavy PP v(vout_heavy) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m
meas tran vo_avg_heavy AVG v(vout_heavy) FROM=0.4m TO=0.6m

operating_conditions.load_current: ~0.1 mA (Rload_light = 18 kOhm) and ~50 mA (Rload_heavy = 36 Ohm), both resistive -- see tb_amp_selfosc.spice
operating_conditions.output_cap: 0.33 uF with 1 mOhm ESR on both branches: the a-priori worst point of DR-0001's window (smallest C_eff, no ESR zero)
operating_conditions.enable_state: EN held at VIN for the whole run -- the transient starts from the settled regulating operating point, so the measured window contains no enable transient
operating_conditions.stimulus: none. Nothing drives either instance inside the measurement window; any periodic content there is the circuit's own.
operating_conditions.timestep_and_window: tran 200n 0.6m 0.3m 200n, measured over 0.4-0.6 ms. The 200 ns ceiling is ~10 points per period of the ~500 kHz activity this bench exists to catch, and it is load-bearing rather than a performance knob: Gear/BDF integration is numerically damping, so a coarser ceiling damps the very signal being measured. Verified by hand at tt/27C/3.30V -- 'tran 400n 0.3m 0.15m 400n' reports 37 nV pk-pk on the heavy branch where this setting reports 3.31 V. The coarse setting is the false negative; do not loosen it to make the matrix cheaper.

bg_pp_light_mv.description: Stage-2 output node BG, light load. A settled, undriven, stable loop sits at its DC operating point; 1 mV is ~3 decades above the integrator's own residue on this node and ~3 decades below the swing a sustained oscillation produces, so it separates the two without being a tolerance to tune.

pg_pp_light_mv.description: Pass-device gate (ERRAMP_OUT/PASS_GATE tie), light load. Same bar, on the node that actually modulates the pass device -- this is the one a consumer of the block would see as output ripple and as excess Iq.

bg_pp_heavy_mv.description: Same as bg_pp_light_mv at the full rated 50 mA load, so a failure cannot be dismissed as a light-load-only condition (and a pass cannot be claimed from the light branch alone).

pg_pp_heavy_mv.description: Same as pg_pp_light_mv at the full rated 50 mA load.

vout_avg_light_v.description: Branch check, not an accuracy check: confirms the light instance is on the regulating DC solution (+/-10% of 1.8 V), so the peak-to-peak numbers above are about the operating point they claim to be about. Accuracy is sim/load-regulation/'s claim.

vout_avg_heavy_v.description: Same branch check for the 50 mA instance.
